sources.title: Neil Armstrong Hall of Engineering
sources.provider: Design and Build With Metal / Arconic project case history
sources.source_date: Project completed October 2007; article page gives project-era description
relevant_evidence: Atrium ceiling is described as 53 feet high.
High roof is described as a warped, wing-like cantilever on both ends and clad in Mayflower Red ACM.
Canopy and vestibule cladding is identified as Sea Wolf ACM.
The atrium is described as housing an Apollo I command-unit replica; the article does not establish current 2026 display status.
sources.method_and_uncertainty: Used the stated 53 ft lobby ceiling as a height datum and converted exactly at 0.3048 m/ft to 16.1544 m. Applied the named finish colors as material evidence. Roof and canopy geometry remains illustrative because no dimensioned elevation was found.

sources.title: Apollo capsule makes a journey to new space
relevant_evidence: Purdue's caption identifies a full-scale Apollo I command-module replica being moved into the atrium for the hall dedication.
The same announcement documents the bronze Armstrong sculpture and lunar boot impressions outside the hall.
sources.method_and_uncertainty: Used to limit the atrium spacecraft representation to a command module rather than a complete command/service spacecraft. This is historical evidence for the 2007 dedication; continued presence in 2026 is unverified.

sources.title: ARMS - Armstrong Hall
sources.provider: Purdue University Office of Emergency Preparedness
relevant_evidence: Describes a four-level facility: lower level, at-grade level, and two upper floors.
Lists building rooms including Lower Level B061/B071, 1010, 1128, 1210, 1331, 2200 and 3331.
sources.method_and_uncertainty: Used as current floor-count evidence only. It does not provide floor plates, facade dimensions, elevations, or exact floor-to-floor heights.

sources.title: Neil Armstrong Hall GIS building polygon record
sources.provider: Purdue official BuildingShapesZip4 ArcGIS FeatureServer, as summarized in the project master building audit
sources.source_date: Source date not stated in project snapshot
sources.crs: EPSG:3857 (ArcGIS layer metadata: WKID 102100, latest WKID 3857). The project comparison uses the campus local approximate conversion, not raw Web Mercator distances.
relevant_evidence: Source code ARMS; source name Neil Armstrong Hall of Engineering.
Feature attributes: NUM_LEVELS=6, CountOfFlo=6, F02=17.3, F03=34.7, R=55; units/field semantics are not fully documented.
Official reference bounds in project meters: X [-189.973557, -27.711566], Y [361.929378, 418.720828].
Project audit shell screening: model bounds X [-172.0, -46.0], Y [370.5, 397.0], AABB width difference -36.262 m, depth difference -30.291 m, AABB IoU 0.3623.
sources.method_and_uncertainty: These are master-audit bounding-box screening metrics, not footprint-boundary errors. The official polygon may include wings or extents not represented by the simplified selected wall shell. The GIS 6-level attribute conflicts with Purdue's 2026 facility description of four levels; field meanings are unspecified, so no floor geometry was changed from this conflict. No plan geometry was changed from the AABB mismatch without source-supported registration.

model_registration.local_frame: Existing source objects are parented to AssetRoot_neil_armstrong_hall with its existing parent-inverse transform. The root remains at [0,0,0]; campus placement was not changed.
model_registration.limits: Rotation, footprint wall plates, site alignment and outer shell dimensions remain unverified.

r1_changes.change: Reduced the atrium curtain wall and south wall from 21.5 m to 16.1544 m, moved the skylight/trusses/lights to match, and withdrew the 19.2 m transom row.
r1_changes.evidence: 53 ft high atrium ceiling in the project case history.
r1_changes.uncertainty: Atrium height is evidence-backed; the model's wall alignment and roof plane remain approximate.

r1_changes.change: Replaced the generic cylindrical Apollo object with a 3.0 m truncated-cone command-module silhouette; hid the separate service module and engine nozzle while retaining stable manifest-listed object names.
r1_changes.evidence: Purdue News Service identifies the atrium display as a full-scale Apollo I command-module replica.
r1_changes.uncertainty: Current display presence and exact replica details are unknown; the modeled dimensions are illustrative, not measured.

r1_changes.change: Applied Mayflower Red ACM material to the high-roof slabs and Sea Wolf ACM material to the entrance canopy and fascia.
r1_changes.evidence: The project case history identifies those named finishes on the high roof and canopy/vestibule.
r1_changes.uncertainty: The roof slabs remain flat proxies and do not yet reproduce the source-described warped wing profile. Material values are render approximations to named colors.

validation: See validation_r1.json. Source was saved, reopened, checked for the stable named collection/scene and object count, then rendered using temporary review-only cameras/lights.
